issues.description: Method PersonService.getAllPersons: the template declares public List<Person> getAllPersons(PersonSortingOptions) (returns a List of Person), and the problem statement describes retrieving a list of Person objects. In the solution, PersonService.getAllPersons(...) is declared to return Set<Person>. At the same time, the solution's PersonResource.getAllPersons(...) declares a return type of ResponseEntity<List<Person>> and directly returns personService.getAllPersons(...). This produces a return-type mismatch (Set vs List) and will cause a compilation error and confusion for students about whether the API should return a List or a Set.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return types consistent. Prefer changing PersonService.getAllPersons(...) in the solution to return List<Person> (preserving the sorted order) to match the template and problem description. Concretely: change the method signature to public List<Person> getAllPersons(PersonSortingOptions sortingOptions), perform the sorting on a List, and return an unmodifiable or new List (e.g. Collections.unmodifiableList(sortedList) or new ArrayList<>(sortedList)). Ensure PersonResource continues to return ResponseEntity<List<Person>> and passes that List through. Alternatively (less preferred) change PersonResource and any client expectations to accept Set<Person>, but the recommended fix is to return List<Person> from the service to preserve ordering semantics and match the exercise text.
